accepted.s: Which committee recommended the Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act in the Andhra area?
accepted.x: The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act was recommended by the Prakasam Committee in 1938.
accepted.tq: Identify the committee associated with the specific legislation.
accepted.sec: AP land reform laws - Ceiling Act 1973, Tenancy Acts, Inams abolition, assigned land  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act primarily abolished which systems in the Andhra area?
o: Jagirdari and zamindari only in Telangana
accepted.x: The Act abolished zamindari and inamdari systems in the Andhra area and facilitated conversion to ryotwari.
accepted.tq: Use the specific reform-object pairing rather than a broad land-reform label.
accepted.sec: AP land reform laws - Ceiling Act 1973, Tenancy Acts, Inams abolition, assigned land  [APPSC]

accepted.s: After the Hyderabad Jagir Abolition Regulation, 1949, jagirs and Sarf-e-khas lands became:
accepted.x: Following the Hyderabad Jagir Abolition Regulation, 1949, jagirs and Sarf-e-khas lands became Diwani, or ryotwari, lands after Police Action.
accepted.tq: Match the abolition measure with the resulting land-tenure status.
accepted.sec: AP land reform laws - Ceiling Act 1973, Tenancy Acts, Inams abolition, assigned land  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Hyderabad (Telangana Area) Tenancy Act, 1950 was enacted in the context of the:
accepted.x: The Hyderabad (Telangana Area) Tenancy Act, 1950 was passed amid the Telangana armed struggle.
accepted.tq: Link a law with the historical movement in whose context it was enacted.
accepted.sec: AP land reform laws - Ceiling Act 1973, Tenancy Acts, Inams abolition, assigned land  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Hyderabad (Telangana Area) Tenancy Act, 1950, protected tenants who had cultivated land for six years acquired:
o: Only a temporary lease for one year
accepted.x: Protected tenants with six years of cultivation obtained heritable rights under the Act.
accepted.tq: Test the qualifying period and the legal consequence attached to it.
accepted.sec: AP land reform laws - Ceiling Act 1973, Tenancy Acts, Inams abolition, assigned land  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A protected tenant under the Hyderabad (Telangana Area) Tenancy Act, 1950 could obtain ownership by paying what proportion of the market price, in how many instalments?
accepted.x: Ownership could be obtained by paying 60% of the market price in 20 instalments.
accepted.tq: Pair the percentage with the corresponding number of instalments.
accepted.sec: AP land reform laws - Ceiling Act 1973, Tenancy Acts, Inams abolition, assigned land  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act, 1956 was enacted on the advice of the:
accepted.x: The AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act, 1956 followed the advice of the Subba Rao Committee.
accepted.tq: Use the committee-legislation association as the deciding clue.
accepted.sec: AP land reform laws - Ceiling Act 1973, Tenancy Acts, Inams abolition, assigned land  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act, 1956, the maximum rent was fixed at:
o: 25% for wet land and 30% for dry land
20% for wet land and 15% for dry land
30% for wet land and 25% for dry land
One-half for both wet and dry land
accepted.x: The Act fixed maximum rent at 30% for wet land and 25% for dry land.
accepted.tq: Watch for reversal of the wet-land and dry-land percentages.
accepted.sec: AP land reform laws - Ceiling Act 1973, Tenancy Acts, Inams abolition, assigned land  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the tenancy provisions of the AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act, 1956?
o: Written leases were prohibited and the minimum lease period was ten years.
Only permanent ownership leases were recognised.
Oral leases were compulsory and leases could not exceed three years.
Written leases were required and the minimum lease period was six years.
accepted.x: The Act provided for written leases and a minimum six-year lease period.
accepted.tq: Combine two provisions from the same enactment without reversing either one.
accepted.sec: AP land reform laws - Ceiling Act 1973, Tenancy Acts, Inams abolition, assigned land  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 1974 amendment to the AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act gave permanent rights to:
o: All tenants who entered cultivation after 1974
accepted.x: The 1974 amendment granted permanent rights to tenants who were cultivating before 1974.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the qualifying period in a tenancy amendment.
accepted.sec: AP land reform laws - Ceiling Act 1973, Tenancy Acts, Inams abolition, assigned land  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the AP Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, 1973 is correct?
o: It applied only to urban holdings and came into force in 1974.
It was excluded from the Ninth Schedule.
It was introduced under Chief Minister N.T. Rama Rao and came into force on 1 January 1973.
It was introduced under Chief Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and came into force on 1 January 1975.
accepted.x: The Bill was introduced under Chief Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, the Act was placed in the Ninth Schedule, and it came into force on 1 January 1975.
accepted.tq: Combine the correct political association, constitutional placement and commencement date.
accepted.sec: AP land reform laws - Ceiling Act 1973, Tenancy Acts, Inams abolition, assigned land  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the AP Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, 1973, the basic unit for determining the ceiling was generally the:
accepted.x: The 1973 Act treated a family of five as the basic unit; the husband’s and wife’s holdings were clubbed.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the family unit under the later Act from the individual unit under earlier laws.
accepted.sec: AP land reform laws - Ceiling Act 1973, Tenancy Acts, Inams abolition, assigned land  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the family unit under the AP Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, 1973:
1. The husband’s and wife’s lands were clubbed.
2. Each major son was treated as a separate unit.
3. One-fifth of the ceiling could be added for each additional family member.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Act clubbed the husband’s and wife’s land, treated each major son as a separate unit, and allowed an addition of one-fifth of the ceiling for each extra member.
accepted.tq: Verify each component of a statutory family-unit formula.
accepted.sec: AP land reform laws - Ceiling Act 1973, Tenancy Acts, Inams abolition, assigned land  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The standard ceiling limits under the AP Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, 1973 were generally stated as:
accepted.x: The standard ceiling range was 10–27 acres for wet land and 35–54 acres for dry land; some references cite 30–54 acres for dry land.
accepted.tq: Read the land-class ranges in the correct order and avoid reversing wet and dry limits.
accepted.sec: AP land reform laws - Ceiling Act 1973, Tenancy Acts, Inams abolition, assigned land  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The prohibition on benami transfers under the AP Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, 1973 related to transfers made after:
accepted.x: The Act prohibited benami transfers made after 30 January 1970 for the purpose of evading the ceiling law.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the operative anti-evasion date from the Act’s commencement date.
accepted.sec: AP land reform laws - Ceiling Act 1973, Tenancy Acts, Inams abolition, assigned land  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A Land Tribunal under the AP Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, 1973 was headed by the:
accepted.x: The Land Tribunal was headed by the Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO).
accepted.tq: Identify the administrative authority associated with the statutory tribunal.
accepted.sec: AP land reform laws - Ceiling Act 1973, Tenancy Acts, Inams abolition, assigned land  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT an exemption under the AP Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, 1973?
accepted.x: Plantations, orchards, religious and charitable trusts, cooperatives and Bhoodan lands were among the exemptions. Ordinary individual agricultural holdings were subject to the ceiling provisions.
accepted.tq: Find the item outside the statutory exemption group.
accepted.sec: AP land reform laws - Ceiling Act 1973, Tenancy Acts, Inams abolition, assigned land  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Abolition of Telangana Inams Act, 1955 was notably delayed because it:
o: Was rejected by the Planning Commission
Was withdrawn after the Green Revolution
accepted.x: Implementation of the Abolition of Telangana Inams Act, 1955 was stalled in the courts.
accepted.tq: Test the specific reason for delayed implementation rather than the purpose of the Act.
accepted.sec: AP land reform laws - Ceiling Act 1973, Tenancy Acts, Inams abolition, assigned land  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the AP Assigned Lands (Prohibition of Transfers) Act, 1977, land assigned to landless poor:
o: Can be mortgaged only to private moneylenders
Can be freely sold after five years
accepted.x: The Act prohibits the sale or transfer of land assigned to landless poor persons.
accepted.tq: Apply the statutory prohibition to a proposed transfer of assigned land.
accepted.sec: AP land reform laws - Ceiling Act 1973, Tenancy Acts, Inams abolition, assigned land  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The AP Land Grabbing (Prohibition) Act, 1982 is intended to punish persons who grab:
o: Only forest land outside municipal limits
accepted.x: The Act punishes grabbers of government lands and lands belonging to weaker sections.
accepted.tq: Identify the protected categories covered by the special prohibition law.
accepted.sec: AP land reform laws - Ceiling Act 1973, Tenancy Acts, Inams abolition, assigned land  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Koneru Ranga Rao Committee was appointed during which period?
accepted.x: The AP Land Committee headed by Koneru Ranga Rao functioned during 2004–06.
accepted.tq: Test the committee’s tenure using the paired years rather than its subject alone.
accepted.sec: Koneru Ranga Rao Committee and National Land Reforms Council  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a focus of the Koneru Ranga Rao Committee?
accepted.x: The Committee focused on assigned lands, confirmation of land rights, tenancy regulation and land records. Corporate farming was not its focus.
accepted.tq: Use the committee’s actual land-rights agenda to eliminate the unrelated policy objective.
accepted.sec: Koneru Ranga Rao Committee and National Land Reforms Council  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Council for Land Reforms was constituted in 2008 under the chairmanship of the:
accepted.x: The National Council for Land Reforms was constituted in 2008 under the Prime Minister.
accepted.tq: Identify the authority heading the national institutional mechanism.
accepted.sec: Koneru Ranga Rao Committee and National Land Reforms Council  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The committee of the National Council for Land Reforms dealt with the subject titled:
o: State Agrarian Relations and Unfinished Task in Land Reforms
accepted.x: The committee was titled “State Agrarian Relations and Unfinished Task in Land Reforms.”
accepted.tq: Recall the exact official title, including its distinctive phrase.
accepted.sec: Koneru Ranga Rao Committee and National Land Reforms Council  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes pre-1972 ceiling laws from the 1972 national guidelines?
o: Pre-1972 laws used the family as a unit, whereas the 1972 guidelines used the individual.
Pre-1972 laws abolished ceilings, whereas the 1972 guidelines introduced them.
Pre-1972 laws used the individual as a unit, whereas the 1972 guidelines used the family.
Both used only the village as the unit.
accepted.x: Pre-1972 ceiling laws generally used the individual as the unit and encouraged benami transfers to relatives; the 1972 guidelines shifted to the family unit.
accepted.tq: Compare the two periods by their basic legal unit and avoid reversing them.
accepted.sec: Land ceiling laws - unit, limits by land class, surplus declared vs distributed  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the 1972 national guidelines, the ceiling for two-crop irrigated land was generally:
accepted.x: The 1972 guidelines prescribed a ceiling range of 10–18 acres for two-crop irrigated land.
accepted.tq: Match the land category with its prescribed numerical range.
accepted.sec: Land ceiling laws - unit, limits by land class, surplus declared vs distributed  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding land ceiling laws in India:
1. There were two major rounds of ceiling laws, in the 1950s and the early 1970s.
2. About 21 States had ceiling laws as of 2020.
3. Less than 2% of cultivable area was redistributed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Ceiling legislation developed in two major rounds, around 21 States had such laws by 2020, and less than 2% of cultivable area was redistributed.
accepted.tq: Check chronology, State coverage and outcome together.
accepted.sec: Land ceiling laws - unit, limits by land class, surplus declared vs distributed  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was an important reason for the limited redistribution achieved through land ceiling laws?
o: Absence of any ceiling legislation in the States
Exemptions for plantations, orchards and mechanised farms
Automatic transfer of all surplus land to corporations
accepted.x: Exemptions for plantations, orchards and mechanised farms reduced the amount of land available for redistribution.
accepted.tq: Identify the implementation factor that explains the limited outcome.
accepted.sec: Land ceiling laws - unit, limits by land class, surplus declared vs distributed  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In Andhra Pradesh Phase II of land ceiling implementation, the government estimated surplus land at about 20 lakh acres but took over approximately:
accepted.x: The government estimated 20 lakh acres as surplus but took over only about 5 lakh acres.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the estimated figure from the substantially smaller amount actually taken over.
accepted.sec: Land ceiling laws - unit, limits by land class, surplus declared vs distributed  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the principal goals of tenancy reform?
o: Compulsory corporate ownership of leased land
accepted.x: The principal goals were regulation of rent, security of tenure and ownership rights for tenants. Compulsory corporate ownership was not a tenancy-reform goal.
accepted.tq: Recognise the standard three-part tenancy-reform objective and reject the unrelated alternative.
accepted.sec: Tenancy reform - Operation Barga, rent, security of tenure, ownership rights  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The rent ceiling contemplated under tenancy reform was generally in the range of:
o: One-half to two-thirds of the produce
One-tenth to one-twentieth of the produce
One-third to one-half of the produce
One-fourth to one-sixth of the produce
accepted.x: Tenancy reform sought to regulate rent by limiting it to approximately one-fourth to one-sixth of the produce.
accepted.tq: Test the specific fraction range rather than the general idea of rent regulation.
accepted.sec: Tenancy reform - Operation Barga, rent, security of tenure, ownership rights  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which practice weakened the implementation of tenancy reforms?
o: Reduction of rent to one-sixth of produce
accepted.x: The use of voluntary surrenders and evictions weakened the protection intended by tenancy reform.
accepted.tq: Identify the implementation failure rather than a formal reform objective.
accepted.sec: Tenancy reform - Operation Barga, rent, security of tenure, ownership rights  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Operation Barga was launched in which State and under which political formation?
o: Kerala under the United Democratic Front
West Bengal under the Left Front
Andhra Pradesh under the Congress government
accepted.x: Operation Barga was implemented in West Bengal under the Left Front government.
accepted.tq: Pair the programme with its State and governing political formation.
accepted.sec: Tenancy reform - Operation Barga, rent, security of tenure, ownership rights  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The principal purpose of Operation Barga was to record the names of:
accepted.x: Operation Barga recorded the names of sharecroppers, known as bargadars, and thereby strengthened their rights.
accepted.tq: Use the programme’s distinctive administrative action to identify it.
accepted.sec: Tenancy reform - Operation Barga, rent, security of tenure, ownership rights  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following benefits was associated with Operation Barga?
o: Ownership only after payment of 60% market price
Non-heritable tenancy and 25% share of produce
Compulsory surrender of all cultivated land
Heritable rights and 75% share of produce
accepted.x: Recorded bargadars received heritable rights and were entitled to 75% of the produce.
accepted.tq: Separate Operation Barga’s sharecroppers’ benefits from provisions of other tenancy laws.
accepted.sec: Tenancy reform - Operation Barga, rent, security of tenure, ownership rights  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Operation Barga is associated with which of the following years in the available accounts?
accepted.x: Operation Barga is cited as launched in 1978; another account associates it with 1977, the year the Left Front came to power.
accepted.tq: Handle closely related launch dates by recognising the two reported year references.
accepted.sec: Tenancy reform - Operation Barga, rent, security of tenure, ownership rights  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Clause (h), relating to rent and tenancy rights in Article 323B, was added by which Constitutional Amendment?
accepted.x: Clause (h) concerning rent and tenancy rights was added to Article 323B by the 75th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1993.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional provision with the amendment number and year.
accepted.sec: Tenancy reform - Operation Barga, rent, security of tenure, ownership rights  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Model Agricultural Land Leasing Act, 2016 was prepared by:
accepted.x: The Model Agricultural Land Leasing Act, 2016 was prepared by NITI Aayog, with inputs associated with the T. Haque Committee.
accepted.tq: Identify the institution associated with preparation of the model legislation.
accepted.sec: Agricultural land leasing - Model Act 2016, first State  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT an intended feature of the Model Agricultural Land Leasing Act, 2016?
o: Access of tenants to credit and insurance
Compulsory acquisition of leased agricultural land
accepted.x: The Model Act sought to legalise leasing, facilitate credit and insurance for tenants, and protect owners’ titles. It preferred leasing to acquisition rather than making acquisition compulsory.
accepted.tq: Separate the enabling features of leasing reform from compulsory acquisition.
accepted.sec: Agricultural land leasing - Model Act 2016, first State  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which State was the first to implement agricultural land leasing in accordance with the Model Agricultural Land Leasing Act, 2016?
accepted.x: Uttarakhand was the first State to implement agricultural land leasing under the model framework.
accepted.tq: Recall the first-implementing State rather than the State associated with Operation Barga.
accepted.sec: Agricultural land leasing - Model Act 2016, first State  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the CCRC Act, 2019 is associated with the issue of:
o: Permanent ownership certificates for all landholders
Transfer of assigned lands to corporations
accepted.x: The AP CCRC Act, 2019 provides for 11-month cards, while a proposed 2024 law concerned tenant entitlement cards.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the existing CCRC cards from the proposed entitlement-card legislation.
accepted.sec: Agricultural land leasing - Model Act 2016, first State  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Kumarappa Committee, 1949 recommended:
accepted.x: The Kumarappa Committee recommended cooperative farming in 1949.
accepted.tq: Match the committee with its specific farming recommendation.
accepted.sec: Cooperative and joint farming - features  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Nagpur Resolution of 1959 made which of the following a party goal?
accepted.x: The Nagpur Resolution of 1959 made cooperative farming a party goal.
accepted.tq: Associate the resolution with the policy objective it adopted.
accepted.sec: Cooperative and joint farming - features  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Cooperative farming failed substantially because it was:
o: Captured by rich peasants to evade land ceilings
Rejected by all small farmers from the beginning
accepted.x: Cooperative farming was captured by rich peasants, who used it to evade ceiling laws.
accepted.tq: Identify the stated cause of failure rather than a general criticism of cooperatives.
accepted.sec: Cooperative and joint farming - features  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding joint cooperative farming:
1. Land is pooled voluntarily.
2. Members retain ownership of their land.
3. Management is elected by all members.
4. Produce is shared according to land and labour contributed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements describe the features of joint cooperative farming: voluntary pooling, retained ownership, elected management and distribution based on land and labour contribution.
accepted.tq: Test the institutional, ownership and distribution features as a complete set.
accepted.sec: Cooperative and joint farming - features  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of joint cooperative farming?
accepted.x: Compulsory membership is not a feature of joint cooperative farming; participation is voluntary.
accepted.tq: Find the compulsory element that contradicts the voluntary character of the institution.
accepted.sec: Cooperative and joint farming - features  [APPSC]

accepted.s: As reported for Andhra Pradesh, the number of primary Cooperative Joint Farming Societies was:
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh had 210 primary Cooperative Joint Farming Societies, with defunct societies being wound up.
accepted.tq: Test the exact institutional count and distinguish it from a nearby distractor figure.
accepted.sec: Cooperative and joint farming - features  [APPSC]
